nccl.d: NVIDIA Collective Communications Library: implements collectives as CUDA kernels that also drive the transports (NVLink, shared memory, IB/RoCE network, or sockets). It is what carries tensor parallel's all-reduces between the Sparks.

rdma.d: Remote Direct Memory Access: the NIC reads/writes directly into another machine's registered memory, without going through the kernel on the hot path and without intermediate copies. The foundation of InfiniBand and RoCE.

busbw.d: An nccl-tests metric: algbw × the algorithm factor (\(2\frac{p-1}{p}\) for all-reduce), comparable to the link bandwidth. With 2 ranks, busbw = algbw.

queue-pair.d: The “socket” of RDMA: a pair of send and receive queues where operations are posted. It goes through the states RESET → INIT → RTR → RTS; the transition to RTR receives the peer's address (GID).

infiniband.d: A high-performance network with its own link layer, switches, and flow control (lossless, credit-based), addressed by LIDs through a subnet manager; the birthplace of RDMA and verbs.

roce.d: RDMA over Converged Ethernet: the InfiniBand transport inside Ethernet frames. v1 stays at layer 2 (not routable); v2 travels in UDP/IP (port 4791), is routable, and uses IP-derived GIDs.

gpudirect-rdma.d: The ability of the NIC to DMA directly into GPU memory (via nvidia_peermem or DMA-BUF). In the NCCL log it shows up as /GDRDMA. It was not observed on the GB10 stack measured in the DS recipe (driver 580.173.02): the collectives went through a host buffer. This is an observation of that stack, not a general claim.

dma-buf.d: A Linux kernel mechanism for sharing buffers from one device (e.g., GPU) with another (e.g., NIC). On the measured GB10 stack (driver 580.173.02), the container reported CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_DMA_BUF_SUPPORTED=0.

hca.d: Host Channel Adapter: the RDMA adapter (an InfiniBand term). In Linux it shows up under /sys/class/infiniband (e.g., rocep1s0f1), with an associated Ethernet interface (enp1s0f1np1).

socket-direct.d: An arrangement in which one physical port is served by two PCIe functions (PFs); on the GB10 each PF is Gen5 ×4 (≈126 Gb/s raw; ~100G practical according to the DS recipe's .env), so filling the 200 Gb/s port requires listing both PFs (dual-HCA).

gid.d: A 128-bit Global Identifier that addresses an RDMA port. In RoCE v2 it is derived from the interface's IPs (IPv4 becomes ::ffff:a.b.c.d); each port has a table and NCCL_IB_GID_INDEX picks the entry — typically 3, but it varies per node.

mtu.d: Maximum Transmission Unit: the largest frame the link carries. RoCE derives its MTU (256–4096) from the Ethernet MTU: 1500 limits it to 1024; 9000 allows 4096.

rendezvous.d: The phase in which the ranks of a distributed job find each other and exchange addresses before creating the communication groups; in torch.distributed, via a TCPStore at MASTER_ADDR:MASTER_PORT.

tcpstore.d: The torch.distributed key-value store hosted by rank 0; the other ranks connect to it for the rendezvous (--master-addr/--master-port).

gloo.d: PyTorch's CPU communication backend (TCP), used for barriers, metadata, and CPU collectives; the interface is chosen by GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME.

canal-nccl.d: An independent instance of an NCCL ring/tree, executed by one CUDA block; the message is split across channels that run in parallel (NCCL_MIN/MAX_NCHANNELS).

protocolo-ll.d: NCCL's signaling modes: LL writes 4 B of data + 4 B of flag per word (minimal latency, 50% efficiency); LL128 uses 128 B lines with 8 B of flag; Simple uses large blocks with a memory fence (maximum bandwidth, more latency).

pynccl.d: vLLM's wrapper around libnccl, compatible with CUDA graph capture; the only all-reduce implementation that works across nodes on the GB10 (custom all-reduce and symmetric memory require the same node).

busy-wait.d: Waiting by checking a flag in a loop instead of sleeping: it responds fast, but occupies a CPU core. In vLLM, SpinCondition.busy_loop_s sets how long the shared-memory reader spins before sleeping.

flight-recorder.d: A per-rank ring buffer of the latest collectives (sequence, operation, state), dumped to a file when the watchdog times out or on demand (FIFO); analyzed with torchfrtrace.

rdma-write.d: One-sided verbs operation: the sender's NIC writes straight into a registered region of the peer (address + rkey), with neither the receiver's CPU nor its kernel taking part. The receiver only notices the write by looking at memory, for example at a flag written after the data.

qp-rc.d: A queue pair of type Reliable Connection: it links two peers with reliable, in-order delivery. TensorFold's one-shot RDMA (b12x's proxy) relies on that order: the 4-byte flag is posted on the same QP, after the data stripe, so it cannot become visible before it.

trilho-rdma.d: An independent path between two nodes, with one HCA (or PF) on each side. With two rails, the transport splits every message into stripes, one per rail. On the GB10, the two PFs of the CX7 port make two rails: in the TensorFold variant, the all-gather of a prompt chunk (32 MB) dropped from 3.5 ms to 1.9 ms.
